articles.authors: Hang Lv, Jie Lin, Rongjun Pan, Haifeng Xu
institutions: Institute of Atomic and Molecular Physics
articles.summary: Both acoustic and optical measurements offer simple, remote sensing capabilities for ultrafast intense laser-induced plasma diagnostics. While optical emission has been widely employed for the investigation of the laser-induced plasma, the acoustic emission as well as its relation to plasma parameters remain unclear. We perform an experimental study to simultaneously measure acoustic and optical emission from femtosecond laser-induced argon plasma. The electron temperature Te and electron density Ne of the plasma are extracted by the analysis of the optical emission, and the feature of the photoacoustic emission is investigated as functions of laser pulse energy. …

articles.title: High aspect-ratio modified layers and single-shot processing: Exploring the capabilities of a 2.8 μ m nanosecond laser for stealth dicing of silicon wafers
articles.authors: Alexandre Sagona, Sara Mondor, François Légaré, Christophe Arnaud
institutions: Institut National de la Recherche Scientifique
articles.summary: In the semiconductor industry, die singulation is a critical step, as poor dicing leads to yield loss. Although mechanical sawing remains the most widely used technique, it becomes inefficient for thicker wafers and induces numerous defects along the cut edges. Laser stealth dicing (SD) has emerged as a promising solution for the singulation of advanced semiconductor packages; however, current industrial implementations mainly rely on 1–2 μm infrared sources. In this work, we investigate the potential of a 2.8 μm nanosecond laser for SD of thick silicon wafers. Experiments are performed on boron-doped 〈100〉 silicon wafers of 650 μm thickness using a 60 ns mid-infrared source. …

articles.summary: Ultrafast laser manufacturing is increasingly used for precision machining, surface preparation and functional surface engineering, but its nonlinear and material-dependent response makes process modelling and optimisation challenging. This review examines machine learning applications in ultrafast laser manufacturing, with particular emphasis on coatings and surface engineering. Existing approaches are compared across process modelling, parameter optimisation, monitoring and intelligent control, while distinguishing nominal process inputs from physically meaningful descriptors and hybrid physics–ML methods. …

articles.summary: We demonstrate a scalable post-fabrication trimming technique for silicon photonic devices utilizing a germanium-doped silicon dioxide (SiO2:Ge) cladding sensitive to ultraviolet femtosecond laser irradiation. Precise refractive index tuning is essential to compensate for fabrication-induced variations in large-scale integrated photonic circuits, enabling improved device performance without active power consumption. By irradiating SiO2:Ge films with 258-nm, 400-fs pulses, we achieve controllable, permanent refractive index shifts (Δn > 0.06) that exceed prior laser trimming results by over an order of magnitude at substantially lower cumulative doses. …

articles.summary: Introduction Facial aging in Asian populations presents unique challenges, as photoaging frequently coexists with melasma, and conventional laser treatments carry elevated post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH) risk. SEM, AFM, particle statistics, and textural anisotropy analysis revealed fluence-dependent morphological regimes. …

To achieve a comparable resolution to primary competing solutions, such as electron-beam lithography, and to improve processing efficiency or throughput, the implementation of costly, complex methodologies is usually necessary. These include specialised material customisation, precise control over light-matter interactions, and sophisticated optical instrumentation. In this work, we introduce dual-layer two-photon lithography (DL-TPL), a new patterning approach that combines dual-layer lithography with TPL. …
